As the river descends and the gradient eases, it begins to swing from side to side, undercutting banks on the outside of bends and depositing sediment on the inside. This lateral erosion gradually widens the valley floor, creating broad meanders and flat floodplains. During floods, rivers spread silt across these plains, building fertile layers over time.
